title: Where to stay in Malta: the best areas explained
seo_title: Where to Stay in Malta (2026): Best Areas for Every Type of Trip
meta: Valletta, Sliema, St Julian's, the Three Cities, St Paul's Bay or Rabat? A local guide to the best areas to stay in Malta, who each one suits and how to get around.
tldr: First trip and no car: Valletta or Sliema. Nightlife and restaurants: St Julian's. Authentic and good value: the Three Cities. Beaches and boat trips: St Paul's Bay and the north. Space, terraces and pools: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex. Countryside and quiet: Rabat near Mdina.
table: Everything on foot, main bus terminus, ferries
Restaurants, nightlife, sandy St George's Bay
Buses, walk to Sliema along the seafront
Five minutes to Valletta by bus or car

sections.h: Valletta: for history and walking everywhere
p: Valletta is the capital and a UNESCO World Heritage city, small enough to cross on foot in fifteen minutes. You step out onto baroque streets, St John's Co-Cathedral and the Upper Barrakka Gardens, and the main bus terminus at the city gate connects you to the rest of the island.
It suits first-time visitors, couples and anyone who wants to leave the car behind. Homes here are inside historic buildings, so expect stairs and character rather than lifts and big terraces.

sections.h: Sliema: for the seafront and an easy base
p: Sliema runs along a long promenade with rocky swimming spots, cafés and the Tigné Point shopping area. The ferry to Valletta leaves from the Strand and takes about ten minutes, and buses from here reach most of the island.
It is the easiest base for families and for anyone who wants the sea, restaurants and transport at the door.

sections.h: St Julian's: for restaurants and going out
p: St Julian's wraps around Balluta, Spinola and St George's Bay. Spinola Bay is lined with restaurants, St George's Bay has a sandy beach, and the Paceville nightlife district is a few streets away.
Stay in the residential streets around Spinola and Balluta if you want to be close to the action and still sleep well.

sections.h: The Three Cities: for an authentic, local Malta
p: Cospicua (Bormla), Senglea (Isla) and Birgu (Vittoriosa) sit across the Grand Harbour from Valletta. They are older than the capital, still lived in by Maltese families, and far quieter. A ferry crosses to Valletta in minutes.
Prices are lower than in Valletta or Sliema, which makes the Three Cities a smart choice for couples and solo travellers who want character.

sections.h: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex: for space in the centre
p: These harbour towns sit between Valletta and Sliema, around the yacht marinas. They are where you find penthouses with terraces and private pools for the price of a smaller flat in the capital, with Valletta five minutes away.

sections.h: St Paul's Bay and the north: for beaches and boat trips
p: St Paul's Bay, Bugibba and Qawra form the holiday hub of the north coast. Boat trips to Comino and the Blue Lagoon leave from the bay, and the sandy beaches of Mellieħa and Golden Bay are a short drive away. A car is useful up here.

sections.h: Rabat and Mdina: for a quieter, rural Malta
p: Rabat sits at the gates of Mdina, the walled medieval city in the centre of the island. It is the best base for the Dingli Cliffs, the west coast beaches and slower days away from the coast.
Gozo, Malta's sister island, is greener and slower. The ferry from Ċirkewwa takes about 25 minutes. Many visitors stay on Malta and visit Gozo for a day, or split their trip between the two.

faq: What is the best area to stay in Malta for the first time?
Valletta or Sliema. Both let you explore without a car, have plenty of restaurants and are connected by a ten-minute ferry.
Where should I stay in Malta without a car?
Valletta, Sliema or St Julian's. The bus network and the harbour ferries cover everything you need from these areas.
Which part of Malta has the best beaches?
The north: Mellieħa Bay, Golden Bay and Għajn Tuffieħa have the island's best sandy beaches. Sliema and St Julian's have rocky swimming spots and the small sandy St George's Bay.

title: Valletta or Sliema: where should you stay?
seo_title: Valletta or Sliema? Which Is the Better Base in Malta
meta: Choosing between Valletta and Sliema for your Malta trip? A local comparison of atmosphere, swimming, transport, food, noise and price, and who each one suits best.
tldr: Pick Valletta if you want history, culture and evenings in a beautiful old city. Pick Sliema if you want to swim, shop and have an easy seafront base. They are ten minutes apart by ferry, so you will see both either way.
table: A few rocky spots below the walls
Rocky swimming all along the promenade
Couples, culture lovers, short city breaks
Families, longer stays, beach and city mix

p: Valletta is one of the most beautiful small capitals in Europe. Staying inside the walls means early mornings in empty baroque streets, sunset at the Upper Barrakka Gardens and dinner a few steps from your door. Museums, St John's Co-Cathedral and the Grand Harbour are all on foot.
The trade-off is that Valletta homes are in historic buildings: lifts are rare, rooms can be less bright, and there is little outdoor space. Evenings are calmer than in Sliema or St Julian's.

Sliema is built for easy days by the sea. The promenade runs for kilometres, you can swim from the rocks in summer, and there are cafés, supermarkets and shops on every street. The ferry from the Strand takes you to Valletta in about ten minutes, and you are a short walk from St Julian's.
It is busier and more modern than Valletta, and homes here are more likely to have balconies, sea views and lifts.

For a short city break of three or four nights, or if this is your first time, stay in Valletta and take the ferry to Sliema. For a week or more, with children, or if swimming is a priority, stay in Sliema and take the ferry to Valletta. If you want a third option with real local character and lower prices, look at the Three Cities across the harbour.

faq: How far is Valletta from Sliema?
About ten minutes by ferry across Marsamxett Harbour, or 15 to 25 minutes by bus depending on traffic.
Is Sliema or Valletta better for families?
Sliema usually works better for families: more space, lifts, the promenade for walks and swimming spots close by.
No. Valletta is lively in the evenings around Republic Street and Strait Street but most residential streets are quiet at night.

title: Malta in winter: weather, what to do and where to stay
seo_title: Malta in Winter: Weather, Things to Do and Where to Stay
meta: Is Malta worth visiting in winter? What the weather is really like from November to March, the best things to do, winter events and how to choose a warm, comfortable place to stay.
tldr: Malta is mild in winter, with daytime temperatures usually in the mid to high teens Celsius, quiet streets and lower prices. It is ideal for city breaks, walking and long stays. Pick a home with good heating and plan a few indoor days for rain.

p: From December to February, daytime temperatures usually sit around 15 to 17°C, dropping to around 10°C at night. Most of the year's rain falls between October and January, often in short heavy showers between sunny spells. The sea is too cool for most people to swim, but walking, cycling and sightseeing are far more comfortable than in the summer heat.

sections.h: Why winter is a good time to visit
p: The streets of Valletta, Mdina and the Three Cities are quiet, flights and accommodation cost less, and you see Malta as locals live it. Winter is also popular with remote workers and long-stay guests, who get the best value on monthly rates.

December brings Christmas lights and nativity cribs across the island, with Valletta at the centre. The Valletta Baroque Festival fills churches and palaces with concerts in January. Carnival takes over Valletta and Gozo in February, with floats, costumes and street parties.

sections.h: Things to do on a winter trip
p: Walk the coastal paths at Dingli Cliffs and the north, explore the museums and palaces of Valletta, cross to the Three Cities by ferry, spend a day in Mdina and Rabat, and take the ferry to Gozo on a clear day. Some boat tours to Comino run a reduced timetable in winter, so check before you go.

Maltese stone buildings stay cool, which is perfect in August and less so in January. Choose a home with air conditioning that heats as well as cools, and consider a cosier place over a big open-plan villa. All our homes have heating, several have fireplaces or fire pits, and our local team is on WhatsApp if anything needs attention.
For winter city breaks, Valletta and the Three Cities are the most atmospheric. For longer stays, Sliema and Msida offer the most services within walking distance.

faq: Mild rather than warm. Expect around 15 to 17°C during the day and about 10°C at night, with plenty of sunny days between showers.
Can you swim in Malta in winter?
A few hardy locals do, but the sea is around 15°C in February. Most visitors save swimming for May to November.
Yes. Flights and accommodation are usually much cheaper from November to March, apart from the Christmas and New Year period.
